summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas Triage Workflows. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: When inefficient queries coincide with CPU or I/O pressure, Atlas documentation points to the Performance Advisor (slow queries and suggested indexes), Query Targeting metrics, the Query Profiler and cursor.explain(), and to indexing improvements. Atlas also documents increasing hardware resources, such as instance size and IOPS, as a valid response. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/disk-io-utilization/

Atlas triage starts by matching the incident time to historical latency or service objectives, recent application or deployment changes, node health, and CPU, IOPS, connection, and memory evidence; correlate these signals before assigning a root cause. (high confidence)

For high disk I/O, compare observed disk IOPS with provisioned IOPS and check the Normalized System CPU chart for a high IOWait curve. Unoptimized queries and one-time events such as index builds can trigger these alerts; optimizing queries and increasing cluster IOPS or other hardware resources are possible responses. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/disk-io-utilization/

The self-managed diagnostics FAQ defines the default WiredTiger internal cache as the larger of 50% of (RAM minus 1 GB) and 0.256 GB. It separately describes filesystem caching and other RAM consumers. This formula corrects the legacy shorthand '50% RAM' but does not prove the effective cache allocation of every Atlas tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

For I/O triage, compare observed disk IOPS with provisioned IOPS and inspect CPU IOWait, then investigate slow queries and index builds. These observations identify I/O pressure; the reviewed sources do not establish queued WiredTiger checkpoints as a necessary signature of cloud-provider throttling. (medium confidence)

Memory triage should distinguish the WiredTiger internal cache from the filesystem cache, and allow for other consumers of RAM such as connections and aggregation or sort work. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/diagnostics/ ; https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-high-wiredTiger-cache.html

A July 1, 2026 Nimbly investigation combines Atlas activity events, per-node connection metrics and application logs to construct a failover timeline. Its attribution of maintenance failure and retry amplification is the author's interpretation, and it explicitly requests MongoDB's official RCA; use the evidence-correlation method without treating the attribution as vendor-confirmed. (low confidence)

A useful investigation sequence is to move from cluster and replication health to slow operations and explain plans, then correlate application and infrastructure context. Datadog describes this workflow for MongoDB including Atlas; Atlas documentation independently recommends metric review and query/index investigation. (medium confidence) Sources: https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/mongodb-database-monitoring/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/

Before treating slow queries as a pure capacity problem, inspect representative execution plans for collection scans, excessive documents examined, and unsupported sorts; improve indexes or query shape and verify latency and work performed afterward. Scaling remains an option when optimized queries still saturate resources. (high confidence)

RTPP exposes CPU percentage, disk read/write IOPS, system memory, current operations and query-targeting ratios; Atlas architecture guidance documents one-second UI granularity. Historical Metrics charts are a separate surface with coarser collection and aggregation intervals. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/architecture/current/monitoring-alerts/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/monitor-cluster-metrics.md

For a lost-primary alert on an election-based replica set, check CPU, IOPS, and connection exhaustion first. If resource metrics are normal, investigate cloud-network disruption; Atlas attempts repair and persistent failures require MongoDB Support. An alert collected during an election can be a false positive, so configure its waiting interval accordingly. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

A first-person Atlas incident account dated June 22, 2023 correlates a scheduled analytical query with disk-utilization and profiler spikes. The operator reports improved query latency after retention cleanup and warns that the cleanup itself raised CPU load and reduced the oplog window. This is a reported case, not a universal diagnosis. (low confidence)

RTPP presents current operations and host hardware statistics. Its CPU, Disk IOPS, and Sys Mem fields describe CPU percentage, disk read/write operations per second, and physical memory usage excluding buffers and swap; the reviewed RTPP reference does not label this CPU field as normalized. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/real-time-performance-panel/

Stored cluster metrics normally use one-minute collection, with replication lag and headroom collected at 85 seconds. A project with at least one M40-or-larger cluster receives ten-second premium collection. Coarser normal metrics average finer reports, while burst equivalents retain maxima; use Max metrics and a narrower incident window to investigate spikes hidden by averages. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30)

Memory triage must allow for filesystem cache and consumers outside the WiredTiger internal cache, including connections and aggregation or sort work. Percona warns that configuring an excessively large WiredTiger cache can contribute to OOM; MongoDB likewise advises against increasing the default internal cache without justification. (high confidence) Sources: https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/advisors/checks/mongodb-high-wiredTiger-cache.html ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/diagnostics/
